unit.why: A deathbed scene: the Besht's last teaching on humility and the self-surrender of the heart, ending with his soul departing on the first day of Shavuot. The narrative is minimal and the teaching dominates.
unit.boundary_note: Borderline with saying_or_teaching; quoted from היכל הברכה. The year שכ"ר is as printed.

stories.start_quote: ובאמת מרן הקדוש הריב״ש טוב קודם פטירת נשמתו
stories.end_quote: ביום ראשון של חג השבועות קודם התפלה
stories.summary_en: Before his death the Baal Shem Tov taught that one should feel 'sold' to the evil inclination, with a broken and humble heart, so that no accuser can rule over him; with these words his soul departed on the first day of Shavuot before prayer.

tags.why: The text is a deathbed scene with the Besht's last teaching.

quotes: ובזה יצאה נשמתו ביום ראשון של חג השבועות
ביום ראשון של חג השבועות קודם התפלה
ואמר בזה הלשון ואין קנה כשתהי׳ לבבכם נכנע
tags.why: The Besht gives an exegesis of the verse as his last teaching.
The text is mainly homiletic, with a thin narrative frame.
The teaching is about the broken, humble heart.

quotes: דיא וועסט זיין דבוק בחיה חיים
tags.why: The promised outcome is cleaving to the Living God.
Accusing forces are mentioned in the teaching, but no angel acts in the scene.
